ORGANIC EXTRACTS FROM FRANCE

We do not use simple plant powders or conventional plant extracts for our product. Instead, we rely on high-quality organic extracts! Both our organic artichoke extract and our organic black radish extract come from France. The plants are grown there under controlled organic conditions and gently processed into extracts. We use 500 mg organic artichoke extract in a ratio of 20:1, which corresponds to 10,000 mg organic artichoke leaf powder per capsule. At 250 mg per capsule, our 3:1 organic black radish extract is equivalent to 750 mg of dried radish.

Artichokes are rich in antioxidants. The leaves in particular are an excellent source of the bitter substance cynarin. Our organic artichoke extract contains at least 2.5% cynarin. Black radish is in no way inferior. Among other things, it is rich in sulphur compounds, which are also contained in our organic black radish extract.

 

SPECIALLY DEVELOPED FOR

  • Artichoke is a powerful thistle which ranks amongst the most antioxidant rich vegetables. The leaves are a great source of different phytocompounds like caffeic acids (chlorogenic acid, rosmarinic acid and cynarin) and luteolin.
  • In traditional medicine, artichokes and black radishes have been primarily used for supporting liver function.
  • The ancient Greeks and Romans regarded the artichoke as a valuable digestive aid.

 

GOOD TO KNOW

  • In the early 1900s, French scientists began to investigate the traditional medicinal uses of the artichoke. Later, Italian scientists isolated cynarin from artichoke leaves.
  • Until the 16th century, women were prohibited from eating them in many countries because they were considered to have aphrodisiac properties.
  • Black radishes were considered sacred in Ancient Egypt. Drawings of radishes found in Egyptian tombs can be traced back to 2000 BCE, and written texts from the Greek historian Herodotus also mention that Egyptians thought that radishes contained high energy due to their spicy, warming flavor. Black radishes were frequently fed to workers building the pyramids to sustain and increase energy levels. Egyptian workers typically ate two meals a day, and while breakfast consisted mostly of bread and beer, their evening meal incorporated radishes

ORGANIC EXTRACTS FROM FRANCE

We do not use simple plant powders or conventional plant extracts for our product. Instead, we rely on high-quality organic extracts! Both our organic artichoke extract and our organic black radish extract come from France. The plants are grown there under controlled organic conditions and gently processed into extracts. We use 500 mg organic artichoke extract in a ratio of 20:1, which corresponds to 10,000 mg organic artichoke leaf powder per capsule. At 250 mg per capsule, our 3:1 organic black radish extract is equivalent to 750 mg of dried radish.

Artichokes are rich in antioxidants. The leaves in particular are an excellent source of the bitter substance cynarin. Our organic artichoke extract contains at least 2.5% cynarin. Black radish is in no way inferior. Among other things, it is rich in sulphur compounds, which are also contained in our organic black radish extract.

 

SPECIALLY DEVELOPED FOR

  • Artichoke is a powerful thistle which ranks amongst the most antioxidant rich vegetables. The leaves are a great source of different phytocompounds like caffeic acids (chlorogenic acid, rosmarinic acid and cynarin) and luteolin.
  • In traditional medicine, artichokes and black radishes have been primarily used for supporting liver function.
  • The ancient Greeks and Romans regarded the artichoke as a valuable digestive aid.

 

GOOD TO KNOW

  • In the early 1900s, French scientists began to investigate the traditional medicinal uses of the artichoke. Later, Italian scientists isolated cynarin from artichoke leaves.
  • Until the 16th century, women were prohibited from eating them in many countries because they were considered to have aphrodisiac properties.
  • Black radishes were considered sacred in Ancient Egypt. Drawings of radishes found in Egyptian tombs can be traced back to 2000 BCE, and written texts from the Greek historian Herodotus also mention that Egyptians thought that radishes contained high energy due to their spicy, warming flavor. Black radishes were frequently fed to workers building the pyramids to sustain and increase energy levels. Egyptian workers typically ate two meals a day, and while breakfast consisted mostly of bread and beer, their evening meal incorporated radishes
